text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- As President Daniel arap Moi led Kenyans in celebrating Madaraka (self rule) Day, key opposition leaders Michael Kijana Wamalwa, Mwai Kibaki, Kenneth Matiba, Raila Odinga, Paul muite and George Nyanja were placed under house arrest for 10 hours to prevent them from organising a separate rally as they had vowed to do.

- A new law to replace the contentious Public Order Act will soon be tabled and debated in parliament. But no "meaningful" constitutional reforms will be held before presidential and parliamentary elections later this year, President Moi says.
- The Kenyan government on Sunday blamed hawkers for the chaos in the capital on Saturday and Sunday and banned hawking in Nairobi's main commercial district.

- Parliament members from the populous Luhya tribe are ready to sponsor a terror gang to deal with opposition leaders insulting members of their ethnic group, assistant minister in the presidency Japheth Shamalla says.
- Former Nairobi City Mayor Andrew Kimani Ngumba dies a day after contesting and losing key post of Nairobi branch chairman of the ruling KANU party.
- Kenyan President Moi and Tanzanian President Benjamin William Mkapa urge international community to assist Laurent Kabila in rebuilding his Democratic Republic of Congo.

- Western nations are likely to seek an early meeting with President Moi and senior Kenya ministers to clarify government promises about the conduct of Kenya's forthcoming elections. Some diplomats are concerned that pronouncements on such issues as voter identification and licensing of political rallies appear to be contradictory.

- Kenya and Rwanda are set to restore diplomatic relations. All that Kenya is waiting for is a formal request from Kigali to reopen the Rwandan embassy in the Kenyan capital, authoritative source in foreign ministry says.
